name: Butter / ghee

image.caption: Cans of Bretel butter with a plate of toast

lead: Butter and ghee are dairy fats that ancestral and looksmaxxing diet communities choose over vegetable oils, linking them to skin health, hormone support and a better physique.

Butter is about 80 percent butterfat, and ghee is clarified butter with milk solids removed and a higher smoke point. They supply saturated and monounsaturated fat and vitamin A. Appearance effects have not been studied; a 2016 meta-analysis found small or insignificant associations between about 14 grams of butter a day and mortality or cardiovascular disease.

paras: People cook with them, add them to coffee or food, and use ghee for higher-heat cooking in place of seed oils. They are used as part of an everyday eating pattern.

Health bodies advise limiting both for saturated fat: the UK NHS advises eating butter less often, and the WHO's 2023 guidance is cited as recommending plant oils over ghee. Replacing plant oils can raise LDL cholesterol, and ghee applied to newborn umbilical wounds has been linked to neonatal tetanus.

social.title: Replacing butter with vegetable oils does not cut heart disease risk (2016)

chain: Dairy fats instead of seed oils
angle.text: Butter and ghee are used in ancestral and looksmaxxing diets as alternatives to vegetable oils, linked by followers to skin health and hormone support through their fat and vitamin A content. Appearance effects have not been studied; guidelines address them mainly through saturated fat.

lead: Butter is a dairy fat made by churning cream, about 80 percent butterfat, and ghee is a South Asian clarified butter simmered until its milk solids are removed [1][2]. In looksmaxxing and ancestral-diet communities they are promoted as alternatives to vegetable oils.

Health authorities cited in reference works advise limiting both because of saturated fat: the UK NHS advises eating butter less often, and the WHO's 2023 guidance is cited as recommending plant oils over ghee [1][2]. A 2016 meta-analysis found small or insignificant associations between about 14 grams of butter a day and mortality or cardiovascular disease [1].
infobox: Butter about 150 C; ghee about 200 to 250 C

paras: Per 100 grams, salted butter has about 717 kilocalories and 51.4 grams of saturated fat, and contains only traces of lactose [1]. Ghee is nearly all fat at about 876 kilocalories, with roughly 62 percent saturated fat, plus vitamins A and E [2].

Replacing olive or sunflower oil with butter raises LDL cholesterol, and direct evidence as of 2024 was described as limited but pointing toward higher cardiovascular risk than plant fats [1]. The 2016 meta-analysis found no strong case for changing guidelines on butter either way [1]. A 2025 study of over 200,000 US adults reported higher cancer risk with more butter than plant oils [1].

Ghee is used in South Asian cooking and in Vedic and other religious rituals [2]. Its high smoke point suits frying [2]. A 2014 study reported higher DHA in ghrita made by a traditional Ayurvedic method [2]. A 2024 food-science comparison of butter, ghee and margarine exists in the literature [3].

Case-control studies in Pakistan in 1991 and 1995 found that applying ghee to newborns' umbilical wounds was a risk factor for neonatal tetanus [4][5]. This concerns topical application, not eating it.
No studies found on butter or ghee as a replacement for vegetable oils for appearance outcomes. Cardiovascular and dietary research is summarised above [1].

timeline.event: Margarine overtakes butter in the US [1].
WHO guideline update advising limits on saturated fat [2].
